name: Newbridge Capital

summary.text: Newbridge Capital was a private equity venture formed in 1994 by Texas Pacific Group (David Bonderman) and Blum Capital (Richard Blum) to invest in emerging markets, mainly Asia; TPG's own account also names ACON Investments as a founding partner. Its best-known deals were the December 1999 purchase of a 51% stake in Korea First Bank from the Korean government, sold to Standard Chartered in 2005 for US$3.3 billion, and the 2004 purchase of about 18% of Shenzhen Development Bank from entities controlled by the Shenzhen city government, the first foreign controlling stake in a Chinese bank. Newbridge was later brought under TPG as TPG Asia.

facts.claim: Newbridge Capital was formed in 1994 when Richard Blum of Blum Capital teamed with David Bonderman, a founder of Texas Pacific Group, on a venture aimed at Asia; Blum was co-chairman of Newbridge. Bain describes Newbridge as a partnership between Texas Pacific Group and Blum Capital Partners, and TPG says TPG Asia began investing in Asia in 1994 through the establishment of Newbridge Capital.

facts.claim: In December 1999 the Korean government sold a 51% stake in Korea First Bank to Newbridge Capital for 500 billion won, agreeing to repurchase KFB loans that defaulted within the following two years (three years for loans already in workout). The Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Newbridge consortium had signed a terms-of-investment agreement in September 1999.
facts.quote: The government sold a 51% stake in Korea First Bank (KFB) for 500 billion won to Newbridge Capital. The government agreed to repurchase KFB loans that defaulted within the following two years, or three years for loans already in workout

facts.claim: Newbridge beat HSBC in a competitive bid for Korea First Bank. Institutional Investor reported that the KDIC felt Newbridge's offer was too low and that the buyer wanted too many guarantees against undiscovered bad loans; it put the price at roughly US$500 million.
facts.quote: the KDIC felt Newbridge's offer was too low and that the buyer wanted too many guarantees against undiscovered bad loans

facts.claim: On April 15, 2005 Standard Chartered completed the purchase of the entire share capital of Korea First Bank for US$3.3 billion, then the largest foreign investment in Korea. Newbridge held 48.56% and used its rights under the shareholders' agreement to require the other shareholders, the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Ministry of Finance and Economy, to sell on the same terms. The bank was renamed SC First Bank in September 2005.
facts.quote: Newbridge held 48.56% of the bank and used its rights under a shareholders' agreement to require the other shareholders, the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Ministry of Finance and Economy, to sell on the same terms as Newbridge

History

facts.claim: On December 30, 2004 Newbridge closed the purchase of about 18% of Shenzhen Development Bank from four entities controlled by the Shenzhen city government, described as the first acquisition of a controlling stake in a state-owned local Chinese bank by a foreign company; initial documentation had been signed June 21, 2002 and the definitive agreement May 29, 2004. Because Newbridge acquired only 18%, SDB continued to operate as a Chinese bank rather than under the regime for foreign-owned banks. Financial terms were not disclosed at announcement; later reports put the price at US$145-155 million.
facts.quote: Newbridge acquired its interest from four entities controlled by the Shenzhen city government ... Initial documentation for the transaction was signed on June 21, 2002; the definitive purchase agreement was signed on May 29, 2004; and the transaction closed today

sources.publisher: Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton (counsel to Newbridge)

facts.claim: Newbridge sold its Shenzhen Development Bank stake to Ping An Insurance; the South China Morning Post reported the sale of its Ping An shares for HK$9.1 billion, and reports put TPG's combined return on the SDB investment at about US$2.44 billion.
facts.quote: The insurer will buy the entire stake held by SDB's largest shareholder, financial sponsor Newbridge Capital, either for cash or through a share swap

openQuestions: Whether ACON Investments was a third founding partner of Newbridge (TPG's account) or whether the venture was TPG and Blum only (Forbes, Bain) is not settled by the sources retrieved.
The year Newbridge was folded into TPG as TPG Asia (2005 per an encyclopedia entry; 'around 2006' per Forbes) was not pinned to a primary source.
The SDB purchase price (US$145 million for 17% vs. US$155 million for 18%) differs between reports; the 2004 announcement did not disclose terms.

A research paper summarized in a search said the Korean government lost KRW 17.6 trillion on the KFB transactions before interest, with KRW 12.6 trillion recovered as of 2011; its URL could not be pinned down and it is not recorded as a fact.
